title: Bounded minimal singular formal primes are eventually extended
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian Nagata ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], complete for the principal ideal $(x)$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], where $x\ne0$, and assume $A/xA$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Fix a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $A$. Let $\Gamma$ be the finite subsets of $\operatorname{Max}A$ containing $\mathfrak n$, ordered by inclusion. For $\gamma\in\Gamma$ put $S_\gamma=A\setminus\bigcup_{\mathfrak m\in\gamma}\mathfrak m$, $A_\gamma=S_\gamma^{-1}A$ (fractions $a/s$), and $D_\gamma=\varprojlim_{j\ge1}A_\gamma/x^jA_\gamma$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Inclusion $\gamma\subseteq\delta$ gives the canonical maps $D_\delta\to D_\gamma$. Put $C=D_{\{\mathfrak n\}}$. Let $\mathfrak s\subset C$ be a prime such that $C_{\mathfrak s}$ is not regular local and $C_{\mathfrak t}$ is regular local for every prime $\mathfrak t\subsetneq\mathfrak s$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-regular-scheme]. Suppose $\mathfrak s\cap A=(0)$, and put $p_\gamma=\mathfrak s\cap D_\gamma$. Let $E_\gamma$ be the integral closure of the domain $D_\gamma/p_\gamma$ in its fraction field [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. If the set $\bigcup_{\gamma\in\Gamma}\{Q\cap A:Q\text{ is prime minimal over }xE_\gamma\}$ is finite, there exists $\gamma_0\in\Gamma$ such that for every $\gamma_0\subseteq\gamma\subseteq\delta$ one has $p_\gamma=p_\delta D_\gamma$.

source.place: J. Nishimura and T. Nishimura, Ideal-adic Completion of Noetherian Rings II, Algebraic Geometry and Commutative Algebra II (1988), pp.453–467. Proposition 1.18, p.460, with P = regularity; Definitions 1.1, 1.2 and 1.4–1.5. The local lifting input for G-rings is the one recorded by lem-per-local-g-ring-adic-lifting.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical], every maximal ideal of $A$ contains $x$. Apply [lem-per-semilocal-completion-singular-components] to all the finite sets in $\Gamma$: every $D_\gamma$ is Noetherian, semilocal and a G-ring, and every transition is regular. By [lem-per-semilocal-g-ring-j2, lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata] it is quasi-excellent and Nagata. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] it is $x$-adically complete, so the Jacobson-radical lemma also applies to it. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power] its quotients modulo $x^j$ are the indicated localizations of $A/x^jA$. The maps and the contractions $p_\gamma$ are compatible by their construction. In particular $p_\delta D_\gamma\subseteq p_\gamma$ for $\gamma\subseteq\delta$, and $x\notin p_\gamma$, since $x\ne0$ and $\mathfrak s\cap A=0$.

source.place: Rotthaus, Zur Komplettierung ausgezeichneter Ringe, Math. Ann. 253 (1980), printed p.223, final paragraph of Behauptung 1: select K_1 over the finite boundary set, retain all components, and stabilize the finite intersections of minimal singular primes. Agent reconstruction for the normalized boundary in Nishimura–Nishimura Proposition 1.18.

proof.text: For any transition $R=D_\delta\to S=D_\gamma$ and prime $q$ of $S$, write $p=q\cap R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal] the induced local map $R_p\to S_q$ is regular. Its closed fibre is regular. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre] gives $R_p$ regular $\Rightarrow S_q$ regular, and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular] gives the converse. Thus a prime upstairs is singular exactly when its contraction is singular. This also applies to $D_\gamma\to C$.

source.place: Rotthaus, Zur Komplettierung ausgezeichneter Ringe, Math. Ann. 253 (1980), printed p.223, final paragraph of Behauptung 1: select K_1 over the finite boundary set, retain all components, and stabilize the finite intersections of minimal singular primes. Agent reconstruction for the normalized boundary in Nishimura–Nishimura Proposition 1.18.

proof.text: Each $p_\gamma$ is a minimal singular prime of $D_\gamma$. It is singular by Step 2 applied to $\mathfrak s$. If a smaller singular prime existed, flat going-down [lem-sc-flat-going-down] for $D_\gamma\to C$ would lift it to a strictly smaller prime below $\mathfrak s$; Step 2 would make that prime singular, contradicting the choice of $\mathfrak s$. More generally, let $R\to S$ be one of the transitions and $p$ a minimal singular prime of $R$. Every prime $r$ minimal over $pS$ contracts to $p$: otherwise going-down would supply a strictly smaller prime containing $pS$. It is singular by Step 2. A smaller singular prime $r'$ would contract to a singular prime contained in $p$, hence to $p$; then $pS\subseteq r'$, contradicting minimality of $r$. Thus every such $r$ is minimal singular in $S$.

Ann. 253 (1980), printed p.223, final paragraph of Behauptung 1: select K_1 over the finite boundary set, retain all components, and stabilize the finite intersections of minimal singular primes. Agent reconstruction for the normalized boundary in Nishimura–Nishimura Proposition 1.18.

proof.text: For every transition $D_\delta\to D_\gamma$, base change by the finite type quotient $D_\delta\to D_\delta/p_\delta$ is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-base-change]. Since this quotient is a reduced Noetherian domain, [lem-exc-regular-map-reduced-target] makes $D_\gamma/p_\delta D_\gamma$ reduced. Thus $p_\delta D_\gamma$ is radical. By [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] it is the intersection of all primes containing it; by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-contains-minimal-prime] the intersection can be restricted to its minimal primes. Step 3 says these are minimal singular primes of $D_\gamma$. Finally, the singular locus of each $D_\gamma$ is closed: apply J-2 in [def-exc-excellent-ring] to the ring itself. Its radical defining ideal has only finitely many minimal primes by [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal], so there are finitely many minimal singular primes.

proof.text: Denote the finite set of boundary contractions in the hypothesis by $\Delta$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal], for every $a\in\Delta$ choose a maximal ideal $m_a$ of $A$ containing $a$, and choose a finite $\gamma_1\in\Gamma$ containing all these $m_a$. For $\delta\supseteq\gamma_1$ put $I_\delta=p_\delta D_{\gamma_1}$. Step 4 expresses $I_\delta$ as an intersection of a subset of the fixed finite set of minimal singular primes of $D_{\gamma_1}$, so only finitely many values occur. They decrease with $\delta$: if $\delta\subseteq\epsilon$, contraction compatibility gives $p_\epsilon D_\delta\subseteq p_\delta$, and hence $I_\epsilon\subseteq I_\delta$. Choose an inclusion-minimal value, attained at $\gamma_0\supseteq\gamma_1$. Then $I_\delta=I_{\gamma_0}$ for every $\delta\supseteq\gamma_0$.

proof.text: Fix $\gamma_0\subseteq\gamma\subseteq\delta$ and a prime $r$ minimal over $I=p_\delta D_\gamma$. The normalization $E_\delta$ is finite over $D_\delta/p_\delta$: use the Nagata property from Step 1 and [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring, def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain], taking the fraction field as its own finite extension. Apply [lem-per-normalized-boundary-component-retention] to the regular map $D_\delta/p_\delta\to D_\gamma/I$ from Step 4 and its minimal prime $r/I$. All hypotheses hold: these rings are Noetherian, the source is a domain, $x$ is nonzero there by Step 1, and its image lies in every maximal ideal of the quotient. We obtain a prime $q\supseteq r$ of $D_\gamma$ containing $x$ and $Q\in\operatorname{Min}(xE_\delta)$ such that $a=q\cap A=Q\cap A\in\Delta$.

source.place: Rotthaus, Zur Komplettierung ausgezeichneter Ringe, Math. Ann. 253 (1980), printed p.223, final paragraph of Behauptung 1: select K_1 over the finite boundary set, retain all components, and stabilize the finite intersections of minimal singular primes. proof.text: The quotient identifications in Step 1 show that $q=aD_\gamma$: primes containing $x$ correspond to primes in $S_\gamma^{-1}(A/xA)$, and contraction followed by extension recovers such a prime. Since $a\subseteq m_a\in\gamma_1$, $a$ is disjoint from $S_{\gamma_1}$, so $q_1=aD_{\gamma_1}$ is also prime, by the same quotient identification. Its contraction to $D_\gamma$ is $q$, since the quotient transition is precisely the localization map and both primes contract to $a/xA$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal], the regular transition induces a regular, hence flat, local map $(D_\gamma)_q\to(D_{\gamma_1})_{q_1}$. It is local, and hence faithfully flat by [lem-pc-local-flat-faithful-flat-reflects-surjective].

source.place: Rotthaus, Zur Komplettierung ausgezeichneter Ringe, Math. Ann. 253 (1980), printed p.223, final paragraph of Behauptung 1: select K_1 over the finite boundary set, retain all components, and stabilize the finite intersections of minimal singular primes. proof.text: Step 5 gives $p_\delta D_{\gamma_1}=p_\gamma D_{\gamma_1}$. Localize this equality at $q_1$ and contract through the faithfully flat local map of Step 7. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], $I(D_\gamma)_q=p_\gamma(D_\gamma)_q$. For $h\in p_\gamma$ this says that some $u\notin q$ has $uh\in I\subseteq r$. Since $r\subseteq q$ is prime, $u\notin r$, hence $h\in r$. This holds for every minimal prime $r$ of $I$; by the radical-intersection description in Step 4 it gives $p_\gamma\subseteq I$. The reverse inclusion was proved in Step 1, so $p_\gamma=p_\delta D_\gamma$, as required.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NV-61dade40b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement and the parent lem-per-qe-rotthaus-finite-boundary. This is a first split of a statement-only node, not a 2026-10-21 re-split. The 8 steps match Rotthaus 1980 p.223 and Nishimura–Nishimura Prop 1.18. (1) Every maximal ideal contains x (Jacobson lemma); D_gamma is Noetherian, x-complete, a semilocal G-ring and quasi-excellent/Nagata. (2) Regular transitions preserve and reflect singularity, by the two flat local criteria. (3) Going-down gives the minimal-singular-prime arguments, which are correct. (4) The regular base change along the finite-type map D_delta -> D_delta/p_delta has a reduced target, so p_delta D_gamma is radical and is the intersection of finitely many minimal singular primes (J-2 makes Sing closed). (5) gamma_1 contains the m_a; the finite set of values decreases with delta, so an inclusion-minimal value stabilises without any DCC. (6) Nagata makes E_delta finite, and new node 2 applies with all hypotheses checked. (7) q = aD_gamma and q1 = aD_{gamma_1}, checked modulo x; the regular local map is flat and local, hence faithfully flat. (8) Faithfully flat contraction plus the u-trick gives p_gamma ⊆ I. Empty Delta is impossible, so it causes no problem. New node normalized-boundary-component-retention is true: I checked a full proof (H = E⊗S is normal by Stacks 0BFK, which I verified at more-algebra.tex:10553; then Krull plus flat going-down). Edge cases are fine, and it is not a duplicate of the smooth-normal-ascent nodes. New node semilocal-completion-singular-components is true: it is the semilocal G-ring lifting theorem (Rotthaus 1979, Kurano–Shimomoto App. A) plus g-ring-completion-regular for the transitions. It is not a duplicate of local-g-ring-adic-lifting, which is local only, and it does not cite the ancestor gabber-adic-quasi-excellence, so there is no circularity. Batch-5 flag: semilocal-g-ring-j2 reaches lem-trf-regular-ring-universally-catenary. That is generic commutative algebra (regular rings are Cohen–Macaulay, hence universally catenary), not trace formula or Poincaré duality content, so I accept it.
